To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the performance of the lossy compression algorithms depends on the signal characteristics.
the compression algorithms have different characteristics for different types of sensors, and hence the selection of the best compression technique is a challenging task.

the compression algorithms are classified based on the signal features of sensor data, the classification is based on the signal type and the signal features are the mean, standard deviation and skewness of the sensor data.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following aspects: a) Analysis of the performance of the lossy compression techniques on the sensor data with different dynamics.
the investigation of the signal characteristics of the sensor data and the impact on the compression gain and loss.
the investigation of compression techniques and the impact of the signal characteristics of different sensors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the compression techniques can be classified into two groups: 1) those that are sensitive to the signal characteristics of the data and 2) those that are insensitive to the signal characteristics.
the compression algorithms perform better when they are used with the data type for which they have been designed for.
the compression algorithms can be classified based on the sensor signal features and hence the same compression algorithm can be used for different sensors having similar signal features.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
for a given sensor type, the best compression technique can be selected based on the signal dynamics.

the compression techniques can be classified based on the signal features of the sensor data and this can be used as the first step for the recommender system to select the preferred compression techniques.
the compression algorithms can be mapped to different sensor signal characteristics.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the compression gain and the compression ratio are highly dependent on the type of signal characteristics of the sensor data.
sensor data with different signal characteristics have different optimal compression ratios.
the compression gain is not only dependent on the compression algorithm but also on the signal characteristics and the data type.
